---
title: Callout title option is not rendered as an HTML title attribute
format:
  html: default
  revealjs: default
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      ensureHtmlElements:
        -
          - div.callout.callout-titled#with-id
          - div.callout.callout-titled.test-data-attr[data-foo="bar"]
        -
          - div.callout[title]
    revealjs:
      ensureHtmlElements:
        -
          - section > div.callout.callout-titled#with-id # no wrapper needed
          - div[data-foo="bar"] > div.callout.callout-titled
        -
          - div.callout[title]
          - div[title] > div.callout # wrapper
---

The `title` option of a callout is rendered as the callout heading.
It must not also be passed through as an HTML `title` attribute, which browsers show as a tooltip over the whole callout.
In html the leftover attributes are copied onto the `.callout` div; in revealjs they go on a wrapper div, so a titled callout with only an id needs no wrapper.
Other leftover attributes such as `data-*` are still passed through.

## Titled callout with an id

::: {#with-id .callout-note title="Titled"}
Body.
:::

## Titled callout with a data attribute

::: {.callout-tip .test-data-attr title="Plain" data-foo="bar"}
Body.
:::
